shm-energy-s1.title: A glider on an air track
shm-energy-s1.html: The glider is pulled to x = +0.12 m and released from rest. Friction is negligible. The system is the glider and the spring.

shm-energy-s2.title: Energy of an oscillating block
shm-energy-s2.text: A block oscillates on a horizontal spring with negligible friction. Sensors record its kinetic energy and the spring's potential energy at four moments.

items.q: What is the total mechanical energy of the glider-spring system? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you left out the ½. Spring potential energy is U_s = ½kx².
Value: you did not square the displacement. U_s = ½k(Δx)².

why.correct: At release the glider is at rest, so all the energy is in the spring: E = ½kA² = ½(50 N/m)(0.12 m)² = 0.36 J. With no friction this total stays the same throughout.

items.q: What is the glider's speed as it passes x = 0? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is v². Take the square root: v = √(2K/m).
Value: you used K = mv² without the ½. ½mv² = 0.36 J gives v = √(2 × 0.36 J / 0.50 kg).

why.correct: At x = 0 the spring has no energy, so K = E = 0.36 J. ½mv² = 0.36 J gives v = √(2 × 0.36 J / 0.50 kg) = √1.44 m/s = 1.2 m/s.

items.q: What is the glider's kinetic energy at x = +0.060 m? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the spring's potential energy at x = 0.060 m. The kinetic energy is the rest of the total: K = E − U_s.
Value: halfway in position is not halfway in energy. U_s = ½kx² goes as x², so at x = A/2 the spring holds a quarter of E.

why.correct: U_s = ½(50 N/m)(0.060 m)² = 0.090 J. K = E − U_s = 0.36 J − 0.09 J = 0.27 J: three quarters of the energy is kinetic at half the amplitude.

items.q: Which statement explains why the glider's speed is the same each time it passes x = 0?
options: With no friction, the system's energy stays fixed, and at x = 0 it is all kinetic
The spring force at x = 0 is zero, so the glider's speed at that point stays fixed
The glider's momentum is conserved, because the spring force is internal to the glider
The period does not depend on the amplitude, so each pass at x = 0 takes the same time

why.correct: With no friction, the only force doing work on the glider is the spring force, which is internal to the glider-spring system and conservative. So the system's mechanical energy is constant, and at x = 0 all of it is kinetic energy.
options: Right: energy conservation with its condition (no nonconservative work).
Zero force at that instant does not explain why the speed is the same on every pass; the energy argument does.
The spring (attached to a wall) exerts an external force on the glider, and the glider's momentum keeps changing direction.
The period is unrelated; the speed at x = 0 depends on the energy, ½kA².

items.q: What is the kinetic energy of the block at moment 4? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is the spring's potential energy. K is the rest of the 0.36 J total.

why.correct: Every row adds to 0.36 J, the constant total. K = 0.36 J − 0.16 J = 0.20 J.

items.q: At which moment is the block at its equilibrium position?
options: Moment 3
Moment 1
Moment 2
Moment 4

why.correct: At equilibrium the spring is at its relaxed length, so U_s = 0 and all the energy is kinetic. That is moment 3.
options: Right: U_s = 0 means x = 0.
At moment 1 K = 0: the block is at a turning point.
At moment 2 the spring still holds 0.09 J, so the block is displaced.
At moment 4 the spring holds 0.16 J.

items.q: At moment 2, what is the block's displacement as a fraction of the amplitude A?

why.correct: U_s = ½kx² and the total is ½kA². At moment 2, U_s/E = 0.09/0.36 = 1/4, so x²/A² = 1/4 and x = A/2.
options: Right: a quarter of the energy in the spring means half the amplitude.
This treats U_s as proportional to x; it goes as x².
This uses the kinetic share (3/4) as if it gave the position.
A/√2 is where the energy splits half and half.

items.q: The block is stopped and set oscillating again with twice the amplitude. What is the total energy now?

why.correct: E = ½kA². Doubling A multiplies E by 2² = 4: 4 × 0.36 J = 1.44 J.
options: Right: total energy goes as the amplitude squared.
This doubles E; it should be multiplied by 4 because E depends on A².
The total energy depends on the amplitude; it is not fixed by the spring.
A larger amplitude stores more energy, not less.

items.q: A block on a horizontal spring oscillates with amplitude A. The same block is set oscillating on a spring with four times the spring constant, with the same amplitude A. Predict how each quantity compares with the first motion.

variables.name: Total mechanical energy
variables.why: E = ½kA²: four times k at the same A gives four times the energy.

variables.name: Period
variables.why: T = 2π√(m/k): four times k halves the period.

why.correct: Total energy depends on k and A; the period depends on m and k.

items.q: A pendulum is released from rest at a small angle. Which describes the energy of the pendulum-Earth system as the bob swings from the release point to the bottom?
options: U_g decreases and K increases by the same amount
Kinetic energy and gravitational potential energy both increase
The total energy decreases, because the bob speeds up and uses energy
Gravitational potential energy stays the same, because the bob's mass is unchanged

why.correct: The bob drops in height, so U_g decreases; with no air resistance and a string that does no work (it pulls at right angles to the motion), the total is constant, so K rises by exactly that amount.
options: Right: a constant total means the gain in K equals the loss in U_g.
With no energy coming in from outside the system, both cannot increase.
Speeding up is energy changing form, not energy being used up.
U_g = mgy depends on height, and the bob gets lower.

items.q: In SHM with no friction, which quantity has the same value at every point in the motion?
options: The total mechanical energy
The kinetic energy of the object
The potential energy of the system
The speed of the object

why.correct: With no nonconservative work done, the mechanical energy K + U stays constant; only how it is split changes.
options: Right: E = K + U is constant.
K goes from zero at the ends to its largest value at equilibrium.
U is largest at the ends and smallest at equilibrium.
The speed changes from zero to its top value and back.

items.q: A 0.20 kg block on a spring with k = 80 N/m passes x = 0 at 0.60 m/s. What is the amplitude of its motion? Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: you did not take the square root. ½kA² = ½mv² gives A = v√(m/k).
Value: you put k on top. A = v√(m/k).

why.correct: Energy at x = 0 (all kinetic) equals energy at x = A (all spring): ½mv² = ½kA², so A = v√(m/k) = (0.60 m/s)√(0.20 kg / 80 N/m) = (0.60 m/s)(0.050 s) = 0.030 m.

items.q: Where in a block's oscillation are its kinetic energy and the spring's potential energy equal?
options: At x = ±A/√2
At x = ±A/2, halfway out
At x = 0, the equilibrium position
At x = ±A, the turning points

why.correct: Equal shares means U_s = E/2: ½kx² = ½(½kA²), so x² = A²/2 and x = ±A/√2 ≈ ±0.71A.
options: Right: half the energy in the spring means x² = A²/2.
At A/2 the spring holds only a quarter of the energy, because U_s goes as x².
At x = 0 all the energy is kinetic.
At the turning points all the energy is in the spring.

items.q: A student says: "At the turning points of a mass on a spring, the energy is zero, because the mass is not moving." What is the error?
options: K is zero there, but the spring holds the energy as U_s
The mass is moving at the turning points, so its kinetic energy is not zero
The energy is zero at equilibrium instead, because the spring is relaxed there
There is no error: the energy drops to zero and is restored by the spring

why.correct: At x = ±A the kinetic energy is zero, but the spring is stretched or compressed the most, so U_s = ½kA², the whole total.
options: Right: zero kinetic energy is not zero total energy.
At the turning points the mass is momentarily at rest, so K is zero.
At equilibrium U_s = 0, but the mass is moving fastest, so K holds all the energy.
The total mechanical energy is constant with no friction; it never drops to zero.

items.q: A 0.30 kg pendulum bob is released from rest 0.080 m above its lowest point. What is its speed at the lowest point? Use g = 9.8 m/s². Give the value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: that is v². Take the square root: v = √(2gΔy).
Value: you lost the factor of 2. mgΔy = ½mv² gives v = √(2gΔy).

why.correct: For the bob-Earth system with negligible air resistance: mgΔy = ½mv², so v = √(2gΔy) = √(2 × 9.8 m/s² × 0.080 m) = 1.25 m/s ≈ 1.3 m/s. The mass cancels.

items.q: The amplitude of a block's oscillation on a spring is tripled. By what factor does its largest kinetic energy change?

why.correct: The largest K equals the total E = ½kA², which goes as A². Tripling A gives 3² = 9 times the energy.
options: Right: energy goes as amplitude squared.
This treats the energy as proportional to A, not A².
The energy grows faster than A, not more slowly.
More amplitude stores more energy in the spring at release.
